However, once I developed ongoing health issues, the level of support dropped significantly.

Due to long NHS waiting times I was referred to a Bupa specialist through my workplace insurance. For about a year, when my consultant prescribed medication, the practice would issue the same prescription on the NHS so I didn’t have to pay private prescription costs (which can be around £150).

Recently the practice suddenly started refusing to do this and became extremely difficult to deal with. I urgently needed antibiotics before going on holiday and explained that I could not afford the private prescription cost. Instead of trying to help, I was told that if you go private you sometimes just have to pay private prices. There was little understanding or willingness to support a patient who was clearly unwell and trying to follow their specialist’s advice.

The situation involved a lot of unnecessary back-and-forth, and at the last minute they decided they needed to speak directly with the consultant, causing further delays.

Unfortunately the reception staff are also often rude, and if you need anything beyond a very basic request the tone and attitude can be quite poor.

Overall, my experience has been that when you actually need support, the practice makes things unnecessarily difficult. I will be moving GP practices and would not recommend registering We are so lucky as a community to have this wonderful surgery and all the people who work in it. I have been with this amazing surgery for over 35 years and have experienced changes of doctors. I have had cause to use the surgery a lot for physical and mental health, especially recently, and I have never once yet had a poor or bad experience with anyone. Fit for work forms are also easy to obtain too.

Unfortunately, through no fault  of their own, rather the government’s, the system for booking appointments has had to change.

It IS harder to speak with someone on the phone BUT be patient and the new econsult and triage service is AMAZING! Or just go down and talk to a receptionist!

If you can’t complete an econsult form yourself ( the surgery provide a paper step by step guide)  you  can get someone else to fill it in for you in your family or the surgery staff will help you, either on the phone or in person.

Once that is done you receive a text message to confirm submission. Your request is then looked at by a designated GP for that day and , if urgent, actioned immediately either by an immediate appointment that day ( my son had an appointment within an hour) or a phone call ( I was called at 6.30 pm by a doctor who recognised my concerns, chatted to me and prescribed medication immediately which I was able to pick up from the late night pharmacy and start taking the SAME night.) If it is not urgent they will send you a message with a link and you can book your own appointments  to suit you - day and time- with your choice of doctor. Their communication is excellent and they just want to help. When you see a doctor, you can book a further appointment then  and there.
